after.text: Activate completion notifications together with the goal background-wait policy (final plan 5.1, 5.3, 6 and 10 stage 2e; leaf 1 of STORY p5-p4a-activation; stacked on landed P4a, relux/main 2f522b9). Until now everything from stages 2a-2d is inactive; this leaf turns it on, for capable hosts only. (1) Host capability: add AsyncNotificationSupport to codex-extension-api, defaulting to Unavailable. Enable it ONLY for verified persistent hosts through the existing extension init (app-server thread processor and thread_manager init; re-locate the plan citations). Headless exec, which shuts down at TurnCompleted, and all its descendants stay Unavailable; inheritance is explicit, and 'not Exec' is not enough. (2) exec_command gains an opt-in `notify_on_exit: true` argument (default false), exposed in the tool schema ONLY when the host capability is Available. Opting in reserves one of the 64 receipt slots before launch and refuses before execution when full (separate from the 64-process cap). Never arm automatically on every yield or stdin poll. (3) New tool `exec_notification` with tagged actions `read {receipt_id, max_output_tokens?}` (returns terminal retained output; not a new blocking or liveness poll; small default; under 10K tokens per item; truncation indicated) and `release {receipt_id}` (disarms without killing the process, or retires retained output, and frees the slot). It rejects stale, foreign and unknown receipts, and is advertised only on capable hosts. (4) Local tool descriptions state exactly what is promised: a wake on exit only when notify_on_exit was accepted, and that release disarms without killing. No promise is made on incapable hosts. Defer any no-wait/end-turn paragraph (it depends on P4b). (5) Activate the P4a goal background-wait policy (enabled where the host capability is Available) so pending opted-in work gates goal continuation. Out of scope: the app-server vertical test (sibling TASK-260929-3f6hfg, F2), P3 capability flags, P4b pacing, P4c subagent wait.

On headless exec and its descendants, neither appears, and passing notify_on_exit there is refused before execution (named tests). AC2 notify_on_exit defaults to false. A default launch creates no receipt, no slot and no wake (narrowing mutant: arm by default). AC3 The 65th concurrent opted-in launch is refused before execution with a clear error. The process cap is unchanged. AC4 exec_notification read returns the retained terminal output with truncation indicated, within the token bound, and never blocks. Stale, foreign and unknown receipts are rejected (one negative test each). AC5 exec_notification release disarms the subscription without killing the process, and frees the slot. A later exit produces no wake. AC6 Tool descriptions match the capability: there is no wake promise when Unavailable (snapshot or string test). AC7 With the policy activated on a capable host, a goal with pending opted-in work does not auto-continue, and user input is still admitted (core suite test). AC8 AsyncNotificationSupport inheritance is explicit, and a child of a headless parent is Unavailable (mutant: derive it from 'not Exec').
